# Environmental and Racial Injustice: Redlined Communities and Pedestrian Safety



## Load packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse) # For R
library(sf) # Read vector 
library(here) # Locate files
library(stars)
library(tmap) # For static and interactive maps
library(janitor) # Clean data
```

# Read EJscreen and Data
 ```{r}
# read in geodatabase of EJScreen data at the Census Block Group level
ejscreen <- sf::st_read(here::here("data",
"ejscreen","EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb"),
quiet = TRUE) 

# Read in geodatabase of EJScreen data at the Census Block Group level
holc_la <- sf::st_read(here::here("data",
"mapping-inequality","mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json"),
quiet = TRUE) 

 # Filter to a state you are interested in
california <- ejscreen |> 
  dplyr::filter(ST_ABBREV == "CA") |>
  clean_names()


# Filter to a county you are interested in
los_angeles <- ejscreen |> 
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME %in% c("Los Angeles County")) |>
  clean_names()

# Find the average values for all variables within counties
ca_counties <- aggregate(california,
by = list(california$cnty_name), FUN = mean)

 ```

 # Part 1: Legacy of redlining in current environmental (in)justice

 ## Histroical redlining neighborhoods
```{r}

m1 <- tm_shape(california) + # Base map
    tm_graticules() +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
    tm_compass(type = "8star",
    size = 3, position = c(
      "right", "top"
      )) +
  tm_shape(holc_la, is.main = TRUE) + # Main map
      tm_polygons(fill =
      "grade",
      fill.legend =
      tm_legend(orientation =
      "landscape")) +
      tm_title(text = "Historically redlined neighborhoods in Los Angeles by grade (Mapping Inequality, 2023)", size = 1)
m1
```
## Create a table
percentage of census block groups that fall within each HOLC grade
percent of census black groups that don’t fall within a HOLC grade in your table
Hint: The HOLC data contains the grades and the EJScreen data contains the census blocks, so you will need to combine the data spatially before doing summary statistics. Once you combine and no longer need the geometries, you can use st_drop_geometry().

### First: check the crs
```{r}
# Check crs
st_crs(los_angeles)
st_crs(holc_la)

# Transform holc
holc_transform <- st_transform(holc_la, 3857)

# Verify
if(st_crs(los_angeles) ==
  st_crs(holc_la)){
  print("it's a match!")
} else {
  print("still not a match")
} # Returned "it's a match!"

# Join the two data
la_join <- st_join(los_angeles, holc_transform, left = TRUE)
```

### Create table

```{r}

census_holc <- la_join |>
  group_by(grade)


```
